title: Stale StyleRuleKey hash after merge_style_rules causes missed dedup and nondeterministic minified output
impact: Silent loss of rules/declarations in a small fraction of builds, varying per process (ahash random seed). Reported via rspack, Tailwind CSS v4 (optimize() -> transform({minify:true}); ~1 in 30 production builds losing styles, PR #1236 comment), Canva (+1 with repro repo), CI rebuild flakiness; 9 +1 on the issue. Present in every release checked (1.29.3-1.33.0 per reporters; 1.30.2-1.33.0 here).
code: src/rules/mod.rs: StyleRuleKey (hash precomputed in new(), eq reads list[index] live, ~line 1198)
summary: StyleRuleKey stores a hash computed at insert time, but Eq re-reads the live rule at list[index]. merge_style_rules mutates rules in place and the cascade merge pops rules without removing their keys, so the map holds stale entries. Effects: (1) deterministic missed dedup when longhands merge into a shorthand; (2) nondeterministic deletion of a live rule when a new rule is pushed at a popped index and its hash lands on the stale entry, making is_duplicate compare the rule with itself.
repro: 1235-repro.mjs. Cases: no-rule-dropped-many-lists-x300 (300 `.pN { &.aN:disabled{...} x2, &.aN[aria-disabled]{...} x2, &.aN[aria-hidden]{display:none} }` blocks; expected all 300 [aria-hidden] rules kept), dedup-after-longhand-collapse (issue body; expected `.x{color:red}.a{border-radius:16px}`, actual `.a{border-radius:16px}.x{color:red}.a{border-radius:16px}`), flat/nested single-list variants, control-plain-dedup.
evidence: Master (src == origin/master, local binding) and 1.33.0/1.30.2 via scripts/repro.mjs --repeat 20: many-lists case WRONG on all, 15-19 distinct outputs in 20 runs (lost e.g. [172,288], [240], [245,264,291]). Direct loop of 50 fresh processes on master: many-lists case lost >=1 rule in 48/50; same 300 copies in ONE rule list (top level) lost in 1/50, nested under one parent 2/50. Missed-dedup case wrong deterministically on local and all releases. Control plain dedup correct everywhere.

fix.approach: Per maintainer review on #1236: drop the precomputed hash and rehash the live rule on lookup with a fast hasher (FxHash), so keys can't go stale by construction; also remove/refresh entries when rules are popped. Benchmark against the precomputed-hash design and keep #1236's tests. Avoid per-bucket scans that go quadratic with CSS modules cross-file duplicates.

openPRs.assessment: Fixes the root cause (buckets keyed by hash_key, live is_duplicate check, index drop/refresh on merge and pop) and has 5 good regression tests, but maintainer (2026-11-21) asked for a simpler design: measure rehash-on-lookup with FxHash; current version is quadratic with --bundle --css-modules (12k files: 228 ms -> 7.7 s). Awaiting author update; mergeable_state behind.

notVerified: Did not build #1236 or a rehash prototype (no Rust rebuild allowed). Note for the requested reliable test: copies with distinct selectors must be in separate small rule lists (separate parents) to amplify; 300 copies in one list fail only ~2-4% of processes. The deterministic missed-dedup case is a 100% reliable test.
